reading_rule: Complete selected scientific source values, with custody-only fields removed as documented. Author-state tokens remain dated source history; original later qualification governs scientific acceptance.

source_record.pair_space_basis: 55 × 54 distinct original property identities, excluding self-pairs. This number is a combinatorial denominator, not an inspection count.

selection.rule: Purposive selection of report-load-bearing relations among function/evidence, dependence/redundancy, detection/containment, diagnosis/restore, repair/support, configuration/experimentation, consumer measures, retries/capacity, preserved evidence/corrective action, acceleration/demonstration and two explicit proxy/ceremony negative controls.
selection.scope: Thirteen unordered pairs, with both directions separately adjudicated. A shared term, source citation or possible co-use is insufficient for admission.
selection.unselected_state: NOT_EXAMINED_AS_PAIR; no scientific negative or completeness claim over the remaining pair space.
selection.native_block_rule: Pair endpoints resolve to the 55 native records and their actual applicable profile families in the current ledger; these labels are descriptive membership, not evidence of an edge.

pairs.selection_reason: Mission semantics determine which events demonstration evidence can count.
The load-bearing redundancy refinement is dependence-aware.
Useful partial detection and containment are deliberately separated from restoration.
Action-sufficient diagnosis can help restoration without root-cause certainty.
Repairability can change a concrete restoration path.
Resources, logistics and authority are distinct from design repairability.
Configuration binding changes the meaning of a fault experiment.
Consumer consequences and service indicators must be related without conflating values with measurements.
Recovery attempts contribute load; capacity conditions constrain retry validity.
Evidence preservation can discriminate a corrective action's recurrence effect.
Acceleration changes which exposure can support a use-condition demonstration.
Negative control: scalar proxy identities and their numerical encodings.
Negative control: cheap-path and worksheet completion do not entail one another.

directions.guard: The named function, exposure and failure predicate correspond to the demonstration question.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Required mission/function and unacceptable states.
directions.intermediate_effect: Determines the event and denominator to which a confidence calculation applies.
directions.receiving_criterion: An explicit population, failure event, exposure and model-bound inference.
directions.remaining_premises: Sampling, censoring, independence/other process assumptions and representativeness.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: A vague mission slogan supplies no event; a well-defined failure predicate cannot make nonrepresentative data representative.
directions.cheap_alternative: A directly observed deterministic function may need only an exact test.
directions.cost_or_interference: More detailed state coding can cost more than it changes the decision.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: A test discovers an observed outcome omitted by the declared function/failure criterion.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Demonstration observations and acceptance mismatches.
directions.intermediate_effect: Exposes an ambiguity or missing state for the mission owner to reconsider.
directions.receiving_criterion: An adequately specified function including the relevant observed boundary.
directions.remaining_premises: The owner must decide whether the new state is actually unacceptable; measurements do not choose values.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: A successful test of an already adequate predicate adds no new mission requirement.
directions.cheap_alternative: Retain the current criterion with an explicit no-change rationale.
directions.cost_or_interference: Chasing irrelevant test anomalies can distort the actual mission.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: The dependence model addresses the same fault set, channels and configuration as the protection claim.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Joint event law or evidence of shared failure causes.
directions.intermediate_effect: Changes the estimated rescue set or invalidates an independence shortcut.
directions.receiving_criterion: A credible bounded redundancy benefit including added failure mechanisms.
directions.remaining_premises: Real joint law, transfer, state, controller and capacity correspondence.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: Perfect shared failure gives no rescue; merely counting replicas gives no dependence evidence.
directions.cheap_alternative: Conservative bounds, one system with repair or a manual spare.
directions.cost_or_interference: More isolation and diverse infrastructure may add maintenance/control paths.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: Observed failures/successes of redundant paths are recorded under comparable exposure.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Cofailure and rescue observations from the architecture.
directions.intermediate_effect: Constrains possible joint failures and directs common-cause inquiry.
directions.receiving_criterion: A dependency claim that distinguishes observed correlation from causal mechanism.
directions.remaining_premises: Sufficient exposure, observation coverage and causal discrimination.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: Cofailure can arise by chance or a common input rather than a shared physical component; a design diagram is not an observed joint law.
directions.cheap_alternative: Retain several candidate couplings and a bound.
directions.cost_or_interference: Instrumentation and rare-event observation can be costly.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: A detected condition is timely and invokes a justified containment action.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Detection of a named failure or error state.
directions.intermediate_effect: Enables selected barriers, isolation or load shedding before propagation.
directions.receiving_criterion: Reduction of the particular propagation path, not full diagnosis or restored mission.
directions.remaining_premises: Action effectiveness, latency, false decisions and unobserved classes.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: Detection without an effective barrier gives no containment; an automatic false action can do harm.
directions.cheap_alternative: A simple direct check and bounded reversible barrier.
directions.cost_or_interference: Alarm burden and unnecessary isolation can exceed benefit.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: A containment boundary preserves or exposes signals relevant to the detector.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: A partitioned fault/effect region with observable boundary behavior.
directions.intermediate_effect: Can localize the signal population and reduce ambiguity or propagation noise.
directions.receiving_criterion: Better-supported detection for the named class.
directions.remaining_premises: Sensor adequacy, signal distinguishability and preservation.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: A barrier can also erase evidence or hide a downstream symptom; containment is not detection by definition.
directions.cheap_alternative: Keep existing detection if the boundary contributes no information.
directions.cost_or_interference: Additional boundaries and telemetry introduce complexity.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: The same supported remedy is effective and permitted across the remaining candidate cause set.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Calibrated ambiguity set plus observed state.
directions.intermediate_effect: Selects a restoration action with a justified conditional postcondition.
directions.receiving_criterion: The stated function/state is restored at the declared boundary.
directions.remaining_premises: Execution, state integrity, dependencies and wider authority may remain unresolved.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: A guessed cause can trigger an irreversible wrong repair; diagnosis alone does not execute restoration.
directions.cheap_alternative: Act on a supported symptom-level remedy and defer exact cause.
directions.cost_or_interference: Extra diagnostic delay can cost more than the information is worth.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: Before/after observations distinguish candidate hypotheses and are not destroyed by intervention.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Documented result of a particular restoration action.
directions.intermediate_effect: Can update the candidate cause set or eliminate a hypothesis.
directions.receiving_criterion: Better-supported diagnosis, still allowing residual ambiguity.
directions.remaining_premises: Confounding actions and unknown intervention specificity.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: Many causes share the same remedy, so success alone does not prove a unique cause.
directions.cheap_alternative: Record that the remedy worked and retain causal uncertainty.
directions.cost_or_interference: Restoration may overwrite evidence; preservation can itself delay repair.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: The failed element is accessible, diagnosable or replaceable by the named means.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Design provisions for access, interchange and verification.
directions.intermediate_effect: Shortens or makes feasible a selected repair/restore operation.
directions.receiving_criterion: Feasible restoration of the required function at the stated resources and conditions.
directions.remaining_premises: Support availability, operator skill, compatible parts and post-repair validation.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: A replaceable module helps little if no compatible spare or authority exists.
directions.cheap_alternative: Replace a whole simple unit if fine-grained modularity adds no value.
directions.cost_or_interference: Modularity can add interfaces, spares diversity and configuration complexity.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: An observed restore exercise or incident identifies an actual access/repair obstruction.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Timed or qualitatively recorded restoration steps.
directions.intermediate_effect: Reveals a design constraint worth changing or confirms current repairability.
directions.receiving_criterion: A repairability claim grounded in the observed operation.
directions.remaining_premises: Generalization across faults, conditions and technicians.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: One successful local restore cannot establish every physical access condition.
directions.cheap_alternative: Retain the current design when the observed path is adequate.
directions.cost_or_interference: Detailed timing instrumentation may be unnecessary for a simple replaceable unit.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: The required spares, skill, access, tools and authorization are available when needed.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: A concrete support capability, including delay and compatibility.
directions.intermediate_effect: Enables the restore path or reduces a named waiting interval.
directions.receiving_criterion: Actual restoration under stated support conditions.
directions.remaining_premises: Failure identification, design access, repair validity and external dependencies.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: Stored spares of the wrong revision or unavailable credentials do not enable the action.
directions.cheap_alternative: Shared support or accepted waiting time can suffice.
directions.cost_or_interference: Inventory, training, travel, obsolescence and maintenance of the support system.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: Restore observations distinguish support waits from active repair and overlapping tasks.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: A trace of the restoration path and resource use.
directions.intermediate_effect: Reveals bottlenecks or unnecessary support provisions.
directions.receiving_criterion: A support plan matched to actual need and consequence.
directions.remaining_premises: Demand forecast, costs and other mission conditions.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: A fast repair during a staffed exercise does not establish overnight or remote support.
directions.cheap_alternative: Keep a documented simpler support arrangement if adequate.
directions.cost_or_interference: Overreacting to one event can create excessive inventory or staffing.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: The experiment's design and observations are tied to the relevant current configuration.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Configuration and changed assumptions of the protection claim.
directions.intermediate_effect: Selects representative fault conditions or identifies obsolete evidence.
directions.receiving_criterion: An experiment that answers the actual current uncertainty.
directions.remaining_premises: Observation validity, bounded risk and test relevance.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: An exact software hash does not establish representative data, environment or authority.
directions.cheap_alternative: Reuse valid prior evidence after a reasoned change assessment.
directions.cost_or_interference: A universal live graph and full retest for every edit can cost more than their value.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: The experiment exposes a configuration-dependent behavior or assumption mismatch.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Fault experiment result under recorded conditions.
directions.intermediate_effect: Refines which changes invalidate which claim.
directions.receiving_criterion: Evidence remains bound to its actual dependency conditions.
directions.remaining_premises: Unexercised states and future changes remain.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: A no-change experimental result need not force a new graph or new action.
directions.cheap_alternative: Record continued support at the tested scope.
directions.cost_or_interference: A risky experiment with no decision value can be wasteful.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: The consumer journey identifies a relevant outcome and a legitimate tolerance-setting process.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Named users, outcome, interval and excluded consequences.
directions.intermediate_effect: Gives the indicator and objective a meaningful target.
directions.receiving_criterion: A scoped SLI/SLO whose denominator and consequence are explicit.
directions.remaining_premises: Accurate instrumentation and actual authority for budget decisions.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: A weighted average can hide a completely failed small group; a stated objective cannot authorize a forbidden loss.
directions.cheap_alternative: A simple binary functional check or no SLO for a one-shot task.
directions.cost_or_interference: Segmentation and monitoring cost can exceed their decision value.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: An observed indicator discrepancy identifies a neglected journey or user population.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Disaggregated SLI data, incident or budget observation.
directions.intermediate_effect: Exposes a possible consumer-consequence omission.
directions.receiving_criterion: A more adequate account of whom and what the service is for.
directions.remaining_premises: Legitimate assessment of importance, exclusions and tradeoffs.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: A metric cannot dictate moral weights or make an excluded loss acceptable.
directions.cheap_alternative: Retain the original consumer model when the discrepancy is irrelevant.
directions.cost_or_interference: Metric optimization can displace unmeasured outcomes.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: Recovery attempts consume the same constrained resource or affect another capacity bottleneck.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Retry/restart rates, state semantics and timing.
directions.intermediate_effect: Changes effective load and reveals amplification risk.
directions.receiving_criterion: Recovery policy remains within a declared capacity/latency regime.
directions.remaining_premises: Queueing, service distribution, admission and nonlinear feedback.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: Unbounded immediate retry at high utilization can push demand over capacity.
directions.cheap_alternative: Stop, delay, shed load or return a bounded partial response.
directions.cost_or_interference: Extra retries consume energy, bandwidth and possibly duplicate transactions.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: Capacity/load observations are relevant to the proposed retry action.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Headroom, backlog, deadline and feedback state.
directions.intermediate_effect: Determines whether waiting, retrying or stopping is justified.
directions.receiving_criterion: A context-valid retry/restart/rollback claim.
directions.remaining_premises: Idempotency, state compatibility, authority and downstream effects.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: Headroom alone does not make a non-idempotent payment retry safe; overload need not forbid all later retries.
directions.cheap_alternative: A finite delayed retry or explicit fail-fast behavior.
directions.cost_or_interference: Overconservative stopping sacrifices useful service.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: The preserved observations bear on the hypothesized recurrence mechanism and comparable exposure.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Relevant failure/recovery logs and state evidence.
directions.intermediate_effect: Enables mechanism discrimination or a later recurrence comparison.
directions.receiving_criterion: A bounded claim about corrective-action effectiveness.
directions.remaining_premises: Valid comparison, changed detection, exposure and deployment fidelity.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: Huge logs without a consumer or consistent denominator do not establish effect.
directions.cheap_alternative: A few decisive observations or honest unknown may suffice.
directions.cost_or_interference: Storage, privacy, processing and service delay costs.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: A specific corrective hypothesis identifies what would distinguish success from recurrence.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Targeted mechanism and effect criterion.
directions.intermediate_effect: Selects which evidence needs preservation.
directions.receiving_criterion: Observability tied to a real decision rather than volume.
directions.remaining_premises: Instrumentation feasibility and alternative causal mechanisms.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: An asserted fix without a falsifiable effect supplies no useful logging requirement.
directions.cheap_alternative: Retain existing adequate records; no new telemetry quota.
directions.cost_or_interference: Overfitting telemetry to one incident can miss a different mechanism.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: Stress preserves the relevant mechanism and the stress-to-use mapping is supported.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Mechanism-specific acceleration model and test observations.
directions.intermediate_effect: Translates exposure or lifetime parameters at stated uncertainty.
directions.receiving_criterion: A bounded reliability inference for the named use conditions.
directions.remaining_premises: Mixture proportions, censoring, model fit and actual population correspondence.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: A single factor applied to two differently accelerated modes biases the result.
directions.cheap_alternative: Use-condition observation or a qualitative bound when transport is unsupported.
directions.cost_or_interference: Higher stress and more model complexity can create a different mechanism.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: The demonstration estimand identifies which mechanism and use conditions matter.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Target reliability quantity, confidence and population.
directions.intermediate_effect: Constrains the accelerated-test question and what must be preserved.
directions.receiving_criterion: A mechanism-relevant stress plan rather than arbitrary test severity.
directions.remaining_premises: Physical model and calibration still need evidence.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: A desired confidence number cannot make an acceleration law true.
directions.cheap_alternative: A narrow unaccelerated deterministic check if it answers the actual question.
directions.cost_or_interference: Designing an elaborate acceleration programme may be unnecessary.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: No general guard establishes the proposed universal conversion.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: A reported MTBF scalar without repair process or mission context.
directions.intermediate_effect: No warranted unique availability/nines follows.
directions.receiving_criterion: A service availability statement requires its own event, interval and repair model.
directions.remaining_premises: All missing process and consumer premises.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: Same availability can have different interruption patterns, and MTBF alone omits downtime.
directions.cheap_alternative: State the particular mean and a separate measured availability.
directions.cost_or_interference: Extra precision or unit conversion creates no new evidence.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: No general guard establishes the reverse universal conversion.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: An aggregate availability percentage.
directions.intermediate_effect: No unique mean time between failures follows.
directions.receiving_criterion: A defined failure process and exposure are required.
directions.remaining_premises: Failure counts, duration distribution, repair and observation model.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: Many short outages and one long outage can have identical availability.
directions.cheap_alternative: Preserve the measured fraction without inventing a failure rate.
directions.cost_or_interference: Relabeling a percentage as a reliability score hides ambiguity.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: A cheap deterministic check is sufficient only for its own actual predicate.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: A low-cost functional observation.
directions.intermediate_effect: Does not prove that all failure modes are controlled or that a worksheet is complete.
directions.receiving_criterion: Failure-mode adequacy/control is a separate claim.
directions.remaining_premises: Coverage of relevant modes and actual mitigations.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: Passing a narrow green check leaves unobserved modes untouched.
directions.cheap_alternative: Use the narrow result as such, without a general FMECA proof claim.
directions.cost_or_interference: Eliminating warranted analysis solely because a check is cheap can raise risk.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

directions.guard: A completed analysis form is not evidence of the cheapest sufficient implementation.
directions.native_bearer_and_input: Worksheet completion alone.
directions.intermediate_effect: Does not establish a direct functional predicate or cost adequacy.
directions.receiving_criterion: An adequate cheap check needs an observed function and relevant acceptance criterion.
directions.remaining_premises: Actual function, failure class and observation.
directions.counterexample_or_nontrigger: A large completed worksheet can coexist with a failing basic function.
directions.cheap_alternative: Perform a directly justified check or record uncertainty.
directions.cost_or_interference: Documentation volume can conceal rather than eliminate operational burden.
directions.quantifier: Conditional contribution only; no universal implication and no complete receiving-property proof.

configurations.name: Direct function check and replace/rebuild
configurations.workable_when: A small system has a directly observable function, tolerable interruption and an adequate replace/rebuild path.
configurations.total_protection: Detection and restoration of the declared simple function; no claim of continuous service or complete diagnosis.
configurations.missing_but_not_fatal: Redundancy, a live dependency graph and predictive modeling may add no relevant benefit.
configurations.incompatibility: Cannot satisfy an unstated continuous-service or irreversible-state requirement.
configurations.cumulative_cost: Low standing control cost; concentrated downtime and rebuild burden.
configurations.maintenance_and_retirement: Refresh the check or rebuild path when the function, state or artifact changes; retire redundant checks after relevance assessment.
configurations.comparison: Can dominate a larger bundle for the stated modest consequence, but no universal cheapest design is proved.

configurations.name: Single robust system with bounded support and repair
configurations.workable_when: Single-channel failure is tolerable and support can restore the function within the stated interval.
configurations.total_protection: A defensible restoration path and support assumption; prevention/maintenance selected only where mechanism warrants.
configurations.missing_but_not_fatal: No claim to survive every component failure without interruption.
configurations.incompatibility: Inadequate when the mission cannot tolerate the supported downtime or local support cannot reach the failure.
configurations.cumulative_cost: Parts, skill, access and validation; less replication complexity, potentially higher interruption consequence.
configurations.maintenance_and_retirement: Maintain compatibility and available skills; remove stale support only after checking latent obligations.
configurations.comparison: Compare actual repair/support burden with additional redundancy, not merely initial hardware cost.

configurations.name: Redundant paths with dependence-aware transition
configurations.workable_when: Some single-path failures are consequential and a second path rescues relevant cases despite dependence and added mechanisms.
configurations.total_protection: Specified tolerated fault set, detectable transition and bounded restored/degraded function; not universal resilience.
configurations.missing_but_not_fatal: Common-cause residuals can remain if the actual protection claim and acceptance decision acknowledge them.
configurations.incompatibility: Shared controller/state/update faults may defeat both paths or introduce more harm than rescue.
configurations.cumulative_cost: Duplicate resources, energy, synchronization, diagnosis, software updates, exercises and support; overlapping controls do not add benefits arithmetically.
configurations.maintenance_and_retirement: Retain current standby readiness/state evidence; change, combine or remove layers when their incremental benefit no longer warrants cost.
configurations.comparison: C02 illustrates positive dependent benefit, no gain, and net loss; it supplies no deployed choice or numerical optimum.

configurations.name: Stateful service with scoped degradation and restoration
configurations.workable_when: A useful partial service and a safe stop can be distinguished under explicit state and consumer criteria.
configurations.total_protection: Preserved named function during selected failures, bounded recovery and evidence for later learning.
configurations.missing_but_not_fatal: Exact root cause, every external dependency and all future recurrence need not be resolved for a valid internal restore or safe partial service.
configurations.incompatibility: Stale search can be acceptable while stale payment authority is not; the same degraded label cannot authorize both.
configurations.cumulative_cost: State validation, consumer measures, retries/load control and evidence preservation can overlap or conflict; optimize only with real decision data.
configurations.maintenance_and_retirement: Keep critical semantic checks current; reassess telemetry and budget policies when consumers, authority or cost changes.
configurations.comparison: Compare explicit stopped service, partial service and full restore under their own consequences; no general fail-open/fail-closed rule.

novelty.basis: Every admitted edge is a conditional contribution to an existing native property. Conjunctions and useful configurations do not automatically create an irreducible new property.

removal_tests.candidate: Detection plus restoration as one indivisible maturity property
removal_tests.test: C12 enumerates detection, safe action, manual restore and root-known variables.
removal_tests.result: Containment can hold without restoration/root knowledge, and manual restoration can hold without detected fault. Neither parent is universally necessary for the other's bounded contribution.
removal_tests.limits: Finite stipulated model, not all physical containment mechanisms.

removal_tests.candidate: Common-cause analysis plus redundancy as a new property
removal_tests.test: Remove common-cause evidence from a numeric protection inference; retain the architecture. Remove the added path; retain a dependency inquiry.
removal_tests.result: The first removal can invalidate a numerical shortcut; the second leaves useful common-cause knowledge. The relation is a guard/information contribution, not an irreducible new bearer.

removal_tests.candidate: Diagnostic certainty plus restoration as a necessary composite
removal_tests.test: Several candidate causes share one supported reversible remedy; remove unique root-cause identification.
removal_tests.result: The bounded restoration claim can survive. Removing remedy effectiveness defeats restoration even with perfect cause identification.
removal_tests.limits: Irreversible or cause-sensitive actions may need more diagnosis.

removal_tests.candidate: Configuration ledger plus experiment as a new reliability property
removal_tests.test: Replace a live dependency graph by a small adequate configuration statement; retain the same supported experiment inference.
removal_tests.result: Representation change alone leaves the criterion unchanged. The contribution is evidence binding, not a new property created by a tool.
removal_tests.limits: The simplified statement must actually preserve the dependencies the claim uses.

removal_tests.test: C12 uses a bijective encoding with unchanged outcomes; C01 retains equal aggregate availability with different interruption patterns.
removal_tests.result: Encoding does not add discriminating power; a scalar relabel does not recover omitted process semantics.
removal_tests.limits: A richer measure can be useful when it genuinely observes additional relevant information.

limits: No cross-lineage or DRF fourth-stage synthesis.
No target repository adoption, deployed experiment, field effect size or cost optimum.
Pure-model contributions are retained even when external correspondence or normative authorization remains unresolved.
Negative controls are inspected specific propositions, not a verdict that the endpoints can never interact.
